newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish bond yields higher, tracking overseas.
newsitem.headline: Swedish bond yields higher, tracking overseas.

text.p: Swedish bond yields rose in line with foreign debt markets while the crown softened in early afternoon trade on Thursday.
The six month T-bill rate rose three basis points to 4.33 percent and the ten year bond yield gained four basis points to 7.15 percent.
The crown was softer at 4.5355 against the mark compared to 4.5210 late on Wednesday.
The market focus was Sweden's imminent announcement on the European economic and monetary union (EMU) and the French elections.
The crown weakened a day earlier on jitters about EMU both at home and internationally. However, some market players said concern about the general EMU process may boost the crown.
"People have begun to understand that general worries about EMU will not affect the crown. Hardly anyone expected Sweden to join EMU in 1999 anyway," one dealer said.
"The situation in Europe is volatile today but the crown really shouldn't suffer if the euro seems like it will be weak. That should actually help the crown," a dealer said.
